caption: Prescriptions can be hard to understand. MedClear explains what is visible; it never diagnoses.
narration: Medicine instructions can be confusing, especially when a label is hard to read. MedClear offers information only, and you should always confirm it with your doctor or pharmacist.

caption: Start with a clear photo. You can upload a picture or take one with your camera.
narration: On the scan page, choose a photo or take one with your camera. The preview lets you check the image before continuing.

caption: For this walkthrough, we’ll load a local sample. It works without sending an image or calling an API.
narration: To keep this demo offline, we’ll use the built-in sample prescription. It loads directly from the app, with no upload and no API call.

caption: Each medicine gets a plain-language card with purpose, instructions, side effects, and cautions.
narration: Here is a medicine card. It brings the visible purpose, how to take it, common side effects, and cautions together in one place.

caption: MedClear calls out details it could not read instead of guessing.
narration: Some parts of a prescription may be unclear. MedClear marks those details openly, so you can check the original or ask a pharmacist.

caption: The daily timeline groups doses by time of day. We’ll mark two sample doses as taken.
narration: The schedule organizes the sample by morning, afternoon, evening, and night. We’ll mark two example doses as taken; these checkmarks are only saved in this browser.

caption: The sample safety check flags a possible duplicate ingredient and recommends asking a pharmacist.
narration: The sample safety section spots two products that may contain paracetamol. Check the actual labels and ask your pharmacist before combining medicines.

caption: It also shows a possible interaction, using cautious wording and pharmacist guidance.
narration: The sample also shows that two medicines may increase drowsiness when taken together. This is a prompt to ask a pharmacist, not a diagnosis or dose change.

caption: Switching to Hindi, then Marathi, translates explanations while medicine names stay in English.
narration: You can view the sample explanations in Hindi and Marathi. Medicine names stay in English to help match them to the packaging.

caption: MedClear is for information only. Always confirm with your doctor or pharmacist.
narration: MedClear cannot diagnose or replace professional advice. Always confirm medicine instructions with your doctor or pharmacist.
